newsitem.title: UK: Mideast VLCCs steady to up, U.S. tankers climb more.
newsitem.headline: Mideast VLCCs steady to up, U.S. tankers climb more.

text.p: Very large crude carriers (VLCCs) in the Middle East Gulf were steady to firmer on Monday, while U.S. crude tankers continued their spectacular climb of recent weeks, brokers said.
Mideast/West VLCCs edged up to W60/62.5 from W57.5 on Friday on rising demand, while to Japan they were steady with the Front Duke fixed at W64 to carry 255,000 tonnes for Toktank, loading April 14.
In the Caribs/upcoast sector, 70,000 tonne crude cargoes climbed to around W235 from W210 on Friday.
"The enquiry keeps coming in and a lot of ships are tied up.
"People are covered to about April 5-6...but I think after Easter we may see rates cooling down quite a bit," a U.S. broker said.
In 1996, 70,000 tonne Caribs/upcoast rates averaged just W148, according to New York-based Rigos Chartering Inc.
In West Africa, there was good demand to South Korea and Taiwan, with the 1992-built Ambon fetching W62.5 to ship 260,000 tonnes to the former destination for LG Caltex, loading April 23.
In the North Sea/transatlantic market, the Berge Septimus was reported fixed at a healthy W77.5 for Statoil, carrying 275,000 tonnes from Norway to the U.S. Gulf.
A lack of early tonnage kept 80,000 tonne inter-U.K./Cont rates buoyant at W140 even though activity was low, with signs that the Med was also rising.

"The Med is slowly following the UKC sector up...We could see W130/140 in the next few days due to a lack of tonnage to April 8," one broker said. Med 80,000 tonne vessels were fixed at about W120 on Friday.
Inter-U.K./Cont 20,000 tonne fuel oil cargoes were unchanged at W200 and cross-Med rates were also flat at W200/205.
